title: A Quarrel at First Light
subtitle: Two greater flamingos rise bill to bill above a flock that keeps on feeding
alt: Two greater flamingos face off bill to bill above a feeding flock on dark blue water
story: Most of the flock has its head down, sweeping the shallows for food in a slow, steady rhythm. Then two necks rise out of the crowd and meet at the top of the frame, bills almost touching.

Whether it is a squabble over feeding space or the start of a display, it lasts only a few seconds. A third flamingo looks on from the back, and everyone else keeps feeding as if nothing is happening.

Low, warm light picks out the pink in their wings against the dark water and the deep blue haze behind them. I kept the frame wide so the confrontation reads as a small moment inside a much larger, calmer scene.

title: Airborne Dispute
subtitle: Two grey herons clash in mid-air while the wetland below carries on
alt: Two grey herons clash in mid-air with wings spread, above flamingos and a standing heron in misty water
story: Grey herons usually stand perfectly still for minutes at a time. This exchange broke that stillness in a burst of wings, legs and open bills.
One heron launches at the other from above, neck fully stretched, while the lower bird twists and lifts off the water to meet it. Water droplets are still falling from their feet.

Below them the wetland barely reacts. Flamingos, storks and a third heron stand in the soft morning haze, which turns the background into a pale wash and leaves the two fighters as clean silhouettes. Moments like this are over almost as soon as they begin.

title: The Running Start
subtitle: Greater flamingos sprint across the water, wings open, to get airborne
alt: Several greater flamingos run across shallow water with wings spread, showing red and black wing feathers
story: Flamingos cannot simply leap into the air. They need a running start, so they sprint across the water with their wings open until they have enough speed to lift off.
This is the moment the group commits: long legs mid-stride, splashes at their feet, and wings that look pale at rest suddenly opening into bright red with black flight feathers.

Each bird is at a different point in the same movement, from the first few steps to the bird on the right with its feet already clear of the water. The haze over the far shore keeps the background quiet so the colour carries the frame.

title: Two Ways to Cross the Water
subtitle: One flamingo flares its wings mid-stride while another walks on calmly
alt: Two greater flamingos wading in blue water at sunrise, one with its wings raised and its foot kicking up spray
story: Two greater flamingos cross the same stretch of water in completely different moods. The one on the left lifts its wings and kicks up a trail of spray with each step; the one on the right walks on, neck curved, unbothered.
Flamingos often raise and flash their wings in group displays, and this looks like one of those moments, though it could just as easily be a bird stretching or finding its balance.

The early sun lights both birds from the side and leaves the bank behind them in shadow, so they glow against the dark background. Their reflections and the line of droplets give the scene its sense of motion.

title: Hidden Colours
subtitle: A glossy ibis rests in still water, its dark plumage catching bronze and green
alt: A glossy ibis standing in blue water, its dark feathers showing bronze, purple and green sheen
story: From a distance the glossy ibis looks almost black, and it is easy to overlook among more colourful birds. Up close and in the right light, its feathers carry a sheen of bronze, purple and green.
This one stood in the shallows with its feathers fluffed, long curved bill resting, turning slowly as the light changed. Each small turn shifted the colours across its back.

I placed the bird to the right and left the open water to its left, so the curve of the bill leads the eye into the frame. The calm blue water and the soft green bank behind keep attention on the plumage.
